theCentralDesignDecision.theDefect: A search surface's default failure is that four different things all render as the same short list, and a reader supplies the missing word by assumption: NO MATCHES (the corpus was searched and the query is absent), NOT ASKED (a region whose vendor is withheld was never queried), NOT PERMITTED (the product refused the read - smart-files' read_outside_scope), and NOT SEARCHABLE (a document that cannot be indexed - no text layer, and the product's own reasons for it). Two of those are facts about the corpus, one is a fact about the caller's permission, and one is a fact about a document.
theCentralDesignDecision.theRule: COVERAGE BEFORE RESULTS. The board draws what was searched, what was not, and WHY, above the result set - so a short list arrives already qualified. This is the one thing a Records search may not defer to a later iteration, because a reader who sees the list first has already drawn the wrong conclusion.

howTheBoardsEnforceIt.Main.dc.html: the at-rest board carries 2 coverage panels, 3 badges and ZERO results - the shape is coverage-then-results with the results legitimately empty, which proves the coverage half stands on its own
howTheBoardsEnforceIt.Results.dc.html: the results board carries 6 results AND 2 coverage panels, both, in that order
howTheBoardsEnforceIt.Gaps.dc.html: the gaps board draws the four sentences apart from each other, with the not-searchable reasons counted under their own reason rather than as a single 'other'

theCentralDesignDecision.noNumberWithoutADenominator: the corpus panel carries the product's own in-scope / searched / per-reason counts WITH emptyCoverage()'s counting rule verbatim, and the illustrative figures are badged as illustrative rather than presented as a reading of a real city.
theCentralDesignDecision.theVocabularyIsTheProducts: the outcome vocabulary is DERIVED from the product's four domain statuses, its read refusal code and its two count words, so a fifth cannot be added by editing a board - it would have to be added to the product first. `reason-not-recorded` is refused as a STORED reason (plant 2) because the product stores exactly three not-indexed reasons and that is not one of them.

theInstrumentThisLaneHadToFixTwiceBefore.oneLine: violate.mjs found TWO REAL INSTRUMENT DEFECTS ON ITS FIRST RUN, and both were the dispatch's named failure mode: a predicate that passes because it matches nothing, or matches the wrong text.

defect1.plant: a coverage panel with its counting-rule element stripped out
defect1.symptom: the plant was NOT caught. check.mjs passed a board whose structured counting-rule element had been deleted.
defect1.cause: the rule matched the counting rule TEXT ANYWHERE in the page body, and the panel's own basis line carries the same words - so deleting the structured element left the text behind and satisfied the predicate. The rule was reading the prose it was supposed to be checking.
defect1.fix: check.mjs now requires the counting rule inside a `data-coverage-rule="documents"` element, and gen.mjs emits that element. The rule reads a tagged element, not a substring of the page.
defect1.whyItMatters: this is the Smart Files precedent the dispatch names - a predicate that self-tests perfectly and matches nothing real. It was caught only because a plant was pointed at it.

defect2.plant: a person's name placed in a table CELL
defect2.cause: the extractor that reads cells keys on the rendered style of the cell spans, and gen.mjs was not applying that style to the case and document result spans - so the extractor matched ZERO cells and every rule over cells was passing vacuously on real boards.
defect2.fix: gen.mjs applies the style to the result spans; the extractor now reads 68 cells across the three boards.
defect2.whyItMatters: the predicate's matched-input count was the only thing that could have shown this. It is now printed on every run and is the number the close cites.

theInstrumentThisLaneHadToFixTwiceBefore.theLesson: Both defects produced a PASS, not an error. Neither would have been visible in a green run. What found them was planting a violation that SHOULD have been refused and reading the result instead of the exit code.

theProof.instrumentOrNot: IT IS AN INSTRUMENT PROBE, NOT A `scripts/surface-probe.mjs` ARTIFACT, and the artifact says so in its own `instrument` field. That instrument measures DEPLOYED surfaces; Records search is NOT BUILT, so there is no deployed surface to measure and none is claimed.

leave_behind: `node _design/smartcity-records-search/violate.mjs` IS THE THING THAT FOUND BOTH INSTRUMENT DEFECTS. Run it after ANY edit to check.mjs or gen.mjs. A green check.mjs proves nothing on its own - both defects produced a PASS.

The matched-input line in check.mjs's output is the only defence against a vacuous predicate. If a count prints 0, the rule over that input is dead and every verdict over it is meaningless. The design's own precedent (Smart Files) is a predicate that self-tested perfectly and matched nothing real.

The probe's gate flip MUTATES _design/surface_coverage.json in place for the duration of two gate runs and restores it in a finally block, asserting the restore by re-running. Do not run probe.mjs while another lane is running the gate; the file is shared.
